description: Report the dimensions, geometric tolerances, and datums that a STEP artifact declares, as data: nominal, deviations, and tolerance form for each dimension; value, zone shape, material requirement, and datum references for each geometric tolerance; and the entity IDs each annotation applies to. `characteristics` checks each dimensional callout against the faces it controls, and reports satisfied or violated where that is arithmetic — a diameter read from the cylindrical faces the callout names — and unresolved with a reason everywhere else, so a callout that was not checked cannot be mistaken for one that was. Check value_resolved before comparing anything yourself. It is false when the magnitude could not be read and is reported as 0.0, which is what a genuine zero callout also reports; a location dimension defining a tolerance frame has no value of its own. A basic dimension comes back not-applicable: it defines a tolerance frame and states no limit of its own. An angle or a location callout comes back unresolved with needs-frame, because the angle between two faces and a location dimension direction both depend on the frame the callout is stated in. A datum reference carries the entity IDs of the shapes its datum is attached to. Without them a tolerance naming that datum cannot be evaluated, so report the datum as unlocated rather than treating the tolerance as met. `unlocated_datums` names those references for you; a tolerance that carries it is not checkable, and saying which datum is missing is the useful answer.Counts report both datum references and distinct datums, because a frame names its references one by one and the same datum appears once per frame. Values are in the declared unit, the same unit this server uses for measurements. Read pmi_kind before describing what a file does or does not declare: `semantic` means the callouts are readable data; `graphical-only` means the file does show requirements, drawn rather than encoded, so say they must come from the drawing or the engineer instead of saying the model declares none; `none` means it declares nothing at all. Use the artifact reference from inspect; entity IDs are valid only for that revision.

include.description: Sections to include: dimensions, tolerances, datums. Default: all three. Example: ["tolerances"].

uri.description: STEP file to read, as a file: URI or an absolute filesystem path.
